stories.title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
stories.summary: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet, a secure way for agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots to complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, allowing its 'dots' AI agents to make purchases for users
sources.text: OpenAI on Friday announced ChatGPT Wallet, a new payment feature that enables its "dots" artificial intelligence agents to make purchases on behalf of users. The company built ChatGPT Wallet in partnership with American Express , Mastercard and Visa , and it allows cardholders to maintain their existing credit card rewards and protections. Eligible users enter their card information once, prompt their dot to find items to buy and approve each purchase with a security check. OpenAI said its dots agents will never actually access a user's card details. Instead, their payment networks will provide the dot with a "payment token," which contains a scoped card number, security code and expiration date that is specific to a given transaction. "Our goal here is to really focus on merchants and our network partners and start building out a really great foundation that's safe and easy to use," Chaya Nayak, who leads product for monetization and payments at OpenAI, told CNBC in an interview. ChatGPT Wallet comes as a growing number of consumers are exploring how to use personal AI agents to manage their calendars, book travel and complete other day-to-day tasks. OpenAI introduced the dots agents during its annual developer conference in late September, shortly after Meta's Muse offering topped the App Store charts . Purchases made through ChatGPT Wallet could eventually kick-start a new revenue stream for OpenAI, but the company said it is not taking a cut of transactions to start. With the initial launch, OpenAI is working to build relationships with merchants and position itself as a serious platform for shoppers, especially as vendors are beginning to experiment with personal agents. OpenAI has pushed deeper into AI-enabled commerce over the last year, but some of its early attempts failed to take off. The company introduced an " Instant Checkout " feature last fall, which it quickly pivoted away from. By March, it had rolled out a revamped shopping experience that aimed to make it easier for users to find and compare products. Nayak said ChatGPT Wallet builds on OpenAI's previous efforts, particularly around product discovery. "We think that this is the next step, where if someone found something they're really excited to buy, then we want to be able to get them through to that endpoint," she said. ChatGPT Wallet is initially available to OpenAI's Pro subscribers in the U.S. who are over 18 years old. The limited rollout is intentional, and the "right approach to make sure things are working," said Luke Gebb , executive vice president and global head of innovation at Amex. OpenAI's ChatGPT chatbot supports more than 1.2 billion weekly active users and nearly 100 million paying users as of the end of the third quarter. With such a broad user base, Gebb said OpenAI can decide to "turn up the volume" on ChatGPT Wallet when it wants to. "It just makes sense to watch it, start it in a contained environment, and then keep rolling from there," Gebb told CNBC in an interview. Merchants and vendors are still reckoning with the rise of personal AI agents, and some companies have opted to forgo them entirely. United Airlines said Wednesday that it will block agents from accessing its systems to book tickets, and Amazon prevents the agents from purchasing products on its platform. OpenAI said Friday that agentic commerce is still in its "early days," and it published tools and guidance alongside its ChatGPT Wallet announcement to help businesses start to navigate the transition. The company explained how merchants can make sure their websites aren't inadvertently blocking OpenAI's agents, for instance. "It's going to take time for the ecosystem to build the right infrastructure to be able to make this experience really amazing and seamless across all of their sites," Nayak said. "Really, who we are speaking to here is the networks and the merchants." WATCH: OpenAI raises $15B at a $1.25T valuation, sources say. What it means for the IPO

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
sources.text: OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents.﻿ OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents.﻿ After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and “eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards.” After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan. After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay , Apple Pay , or Google Wallet , it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. Eventually, OpenAI says it expects “users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases.” ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere. Some retailers have restrictions on AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents. OpenAI says that in order for agents to use ChatGPT Wallet, “websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.”

sources.name: SiliconANGLE
sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
sources.text: Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too! In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China. Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role. However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately . Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top. More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway. The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions of Jensen fanboys and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem. A lot of people are hoping desperately that he didn’t just pop the AI bubble (though others are hoping he did). It seems unlikely this will be the pin, but we’re dealing with a lot of unlikely things in the past week or so, for better and worse, and this shock is clearly rattling the foundations. All that managed to overshadow what otherwise would be the big news this week: Anthropic went on the road to pitch its initial public offering . It’s hoping to raise more than $64 billion and keep the AI trade humming in Nvidia’s near-term absence. Looks like next Thursday is the big day. And it’s not the only good news in AI — that is, if the IPO is successful. After a difficult month on the stock front, uber neocloud CoreWeave provided a pleasant AI surprise with upside earnings and guidance, lifting its shares almost 25% Wednesday. AI chipmaker Cerebras’ shares rose almost 18% in late trading Thursday on positive guidance and a Microsoft deal . Cisco Systems said demand is strong for AI infrastructure, even if investors shrugged, and chipmaking equipment supplier Applied Materials said AI boosted demand as well. Not everyone fared so well, though. Dutch neocloud Nebius saw its shares drop almost 17% Thursday as it lowered its outlook despite close to sevenfold revenue growth in the last quarter. The stock drop no doubt was partly because of Nvidia, which is, of course, an investor. CoreWeave –yes, another Nvidia investment — lost 7% Thursday. Sovereignty is on many enterprise buyers’ lips these days, the notion that enterprises need a way to assert more control over their technology estates and protect their customers’ data. TheCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin just completed the first of a series of reports on how to approach sovereignty, this one focused on the hyperscale cloud providers. The software orchestrator Kubernetes has become boring, but as SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier said at this week’s KubeCon in Salt Lake City, that means it’s a success — with lessons for AI developers. “A lot of things that are happening in cloud-native that were involved in microservices in Kubernetes world are actually the same challenges in the AI world,” he noted. IBM has been working hard on quantum computing for a long time now, but at its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week, it showed significant progress, according to Dave Vellante. Its goal now is to show actual industry impact by 2028, a laudable goal that presents a lot of challenges, Dave said in his Special Breaking Analysis this week. Next week the SC26 high-performance computing conference comes to Chicago, and theCUBE and theCUBE Research will be onsite with interviews and analysis. There’s also Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco. And earnings next week include… Nvidia! Bring the popcorn. Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news, most of it not salacious, along with analysis and commentary from SiliconANGLE and beyond: Breaking Analysis: Sovereign or not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide Breaking Analysis: AI cyber resilience and the trust gap Dario goes overboard with AI claims ahead of Anthropic’s IPO — the same guy who says AI could also extinguish us. Somebody give him back his Xanax! Also, I really don’t think mental illness is a compute problem. Gartner forecasts AI infrastructure spending to represent 59% of total global AI spending in 2027 Gartner also forecasts AI will drive a net increase of 1.7M jobs by 2030 That one number hides a lot of job losses and especially job “transformations,” and not to throw shade on Gartner in particular, anyone betting on AI’s impact out in 2030 is barely more than guessing. sources.name: Xataka
sources.title: Donald Trump intentó que Jensen Huang siguiera como CEO: “Nvidia es demasiado grande como para caer”
sources.text: Nvidia, la empresa que se ha convertido por méritos propios en el pegamento de la inteligencia artificial, se ha quedado sin su fundador y CEO . Estados Unidos y la propia Nvidia podían aguantar que Jensen hubiese sido víctima de una supuesta espía china , pero por políticas internas y tras conocerse otras dos relaciones extramatrimoniales con empleadas, el CEO anunció su dimisión. Ahora, el New York Times apunta que Donald Trump lleva días convenciendo a Jensen Huang para que luche por su puesto. Y tiene todo el sentido si tenemos en cuenta que Jensen, aparte del CEO de Nvidia, era una pieza geopolítica clave para el actual Gobierno estadounidense. En corto . El Times cita a dos personas relacionadas con una conversación entre Trump y Huang que se produjo en plena tormenta. El pasado martes 10 de noviembre, el presidente le pidió que siguiera luchando por su puesto de CEO. No surtió efecto porque, como decimos, una cosa era ser objeto de una supuesta trama de espionaje y otra muy distinta el incumplir normas de su compañía. A comienzos de esta semana supimos que Jensen había mantenido relaciones con la vicepresidenta de salud de Nvidia, momento en el que la junta se reunió para decidir si lo destituían o no. El asunto escaló rápido porque, horas después, el propio Jensen dimitió ... y hace apenas unas horas, Reuters informaba sobre una segunda empleada de Nvidia con la que Jensen habría tenido relaciones. Demasiado grande para caer . El motivo de la llamada y de la petición de Trump es estratégico. Estos últimos años hemos visto a ambos muy unidos, con Huang pasando de ser un "simple" CEO de una tecnológica a convertirse en una especie de mano derecha en cuestiones de Estado. Ha acompañado a otros CEO en las galas de la Casa Blanca, ha recibido medallas por parte del Gobierno y ha estado al lado de Trump en viajes clave, como el de hace unos meses a China. Nvidia es, además, una de las mayores empresas del mundo por capitalización y el puntal sobre el que Trump quiere construir esa superioridad tecnológica estadounidense. No deja de ser la que crea los chips más potentes para la IA y la que alimenta a prácticamente todas las Big Tech relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial. Según estas fuentes del Times, Trump ve el escándalo como un "simple caso de adulterio" y, también según gente de su entorno, Jensen era una especie de Henry Ford del siglo XXI gracias a que su contribución a los centros de datos podían dar un nuevo impulso industrial al país. De hecho, según estas fuentes, el motivo es uno que se ha repetido en numerosas ocasiones estos últimos meses cuando hablábamos de la industria de la IA y de todo el gasto en esta tecnología : "Nvidia es demasiado grande para caer". Aliado . La relación entre ambos en el primer mandato del presidente no fue tan estrecha, pero algo cambió cuando Trump se enteró de que Nvidia controlaba el 80% del mercado de los chips de IA avanzados. A partir de ahí, el mandamás de la tecnológica se convirtió en pieza clave para el presidente de EEUU, siendo intermediario en inversiones gigantescas en infraestructura en suelo estadounidense como en compras internacionales. Un ejemplo es el acuerdo entre Arabia Saudí y Emiratos Árabes Unidos para que compraran chips estadounidenses o, quizá, el caso más sonado: cuando Huang, tras meses de insistencia, consiguió que Trump accediera a vender tarjetas H200 a China . Hasta entonces, el Gobierno vetaba esas ventas porque no querían 'armar' al país que era (y es) el rival tecnológico y comercial, pero acordaron la venta previo arancel del 25% a los equipos como una forma de hacer que China dependa de Estados Unidos a nivel tecnológico. Al menos hasta que la tecnología de gigantes como Huawei se ponga a la par. Reconstrucción . Todo esto no deja de ser información del New York Times y, como suele ocurrir, hay que confiar en las fuentes porque todo se está desarrollando a un ritmo vertiginoso, pero tiene todo el sentido que a Trump no le interese un Huang fuera de Nvidia. De hecho, parece que las agencias estadounidenses ya sabían lo de la relación entre la supuesta espía y Huang y decidieron ocultárselo a la víctima porque Nvidia seguía siendo extremadamente útil. Ahora, toca reconstruir Nvidia , que ya tiene presidenta interina y busca sustituto para Huang. Trump ha mencionado que Tim Cook, que se acaba de jubilar en Apple, sería un candidato ideal y, de nuevo y a riesgo de quemar el meme de Xataka, tiene sentido: Cook es otra persona muy cercana al presidente, es de su confianza, estuvo hasta hace nada en la otra gran empresa del país, es alguien que ha mantenido buenas relaciones con China y con la taiwanesa TSMC. Pero claro, una cosa es lo que quiera Trump... y otra lo que termine haciendo Nvidia. Adulterio aparte, el agujero que deja Huang va a ser muy difícil de llenar. En Xataka | Más de 16 horas de caída de Outlook y Teams, y Microsoft todavía no sabe qué la ha provocado

sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: Nvidia consulta CEO da Arm para cargo de Jensen Huang, diz jornal
sources.text: A Nvidia já tem ao menos uma pessoa em mente para o cargo de CEO após a renúncia de Jensen Huang. De acordo com o Financial Times , o nome de Rene Haas surge como candidato em potencial, embora nenhuma decisão tenha sido tomada por enquanto. O executivo é CEO da empresa britânica de semicondutores Arm , especializada em montar projetos de arquitetura de chips para outras empresas. Haas ocupa o cargo desde fevereiro de 2022. A atual empresa mais valiosa do mundo está sem gerente executivo fixo desde quinta-feira (12) , quando Huang renunciou após a divulgação de dois casos extraconjugais mantidos pelo executivo. Atualmente, a marca é comandada por uma CEO interina, Colette Kress , que também é CFO da Nvidia. Até agora, nomes externos não haviam sido considerados e até mesmo executivos da Nvidia eram pouco especulados como sucessores — Huang era um dos cofundadores da marca e ocupava de forma estável o cargo de gerência executiva desde 1993. Nvidia e Arm foram procuradas pela reportagem original, mas não se manifestaram sobre o assunto. À CNBC , a Nvidia afirmou que está “em processo de seleção de uma empresa de recrutamento para o cargo de CEO” e negou que tenha entrado “em contato com nenhum candidato em potencial” . Haas já tem familiaridade com a Nvidia por mais de um motivo. Ele trabalhou na companhia ao longo de sete anos na década de 2000 , chegando ao cargo de vice-presidente e gerente geral da divisão de computação. Em 2013, o executivo trocou a companhia pela rival Arm. Curiosamente, a trajetória de ambas as empresas quase se juntou tempos depois: em 2021, a Nvidia chegou a anunciar a aquisição da Arm por US$ 40 bilhões. Porém, a negociação foi desfeita em fevereiro do ano seguinte , após a dupla não conseguir a aprovação de órgãos reguladores. A compra recebeu pressão inclusive de fabricantes de eletrônicos, que temiam que a fusão prejudicasse a concorrência no mercado. A Arm seguiu independente e realizou a oferta pública de ações em 2023. A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? Entenda aqui o que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang. /Com informações de Financial Times . stories.title: Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains
stories.summary: We’re bringing clean manufacturing to our data centers and setting an industry standard by entering long-term purchase agreements with low-carbon producers across our supply chain. The post Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains appeared first on Meta Newsroom .

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.title: Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains
sources.text: Today, we’re sharing a new set of long-term purchase commitments spanning cement, steel, trucking, and recycled plastics. Through these commitments, we’re helping bring clean manufacturing to a commercial scale in the industries that build and supply our data centers. Building the physical infrastructure that supports Meta technologies takes significant quantities of foundation materials: cement, steel, plastics, and the freight networks that move them. Reducing the emissions associated with building infrastructure requires not only sourcing differently but bringing lower carbon materials and services into existence at commercial scale. Our multi-year commitments give suppliers the revenue certainty they need to build these solutions, and stepping in early helps demonstrate these technologies so the broader market can adopt them. These agreements build on a track record of testing, validating, and scaling lower carbon infrastructure solutions across our data center footprint. That includes piloting mass timber architecture to replace traditional carbon-intensive materials, open-sourcing AI models to design faster-curing, lower carbon concrete formulations , and joining industry peers as a founding partner of the Data Center Innovation Initiative . We’ve signed a multi-year agreement with Sublime Systems to support at least 180,000 tons of lower carbon cement production. Our support enables Sublime to build its first commercial-scale facility and gives us priority access to use Sublime Cement ® in our data center construction pipeline. We’ve also signed an agreement with lower carbon cement producer Fortera to support a new plant in Ste. Genevieve, Missouri. Both companies expect their early plants to add domestic capacity for lower carbon cement and create new American jobs. These agreements build on earlier lower carbon concrete projects with partners like CarbonBuilt and CarbiCrete . Last year, we signed a multi-year agreement to support domestic clean iron from Electra ’s first demonstration plant in Jefferson County, Colorado. We’re now taking that work from iron into steel: a new multi-year agreement with Sweden-based Stegra supports near-zero-emission primary steel, produced through a process that eliminates coal entirely from iron reduction. Structural steel reaches our data centers through global supply chains. Supporting a first-of-its-kind facility through its production ramp helps validate technologies that can scale across the global steel industry. Building on initial zero-emission freight partnerships with NFI in Virginia and Nevoya (with the Center for Green Market Activation) in Texas, we’re expanding our work with Nevoya to now include a California and Arizona route along the I-10 interstate. Electric trucks produce zero tailpipe emissions and run quieter than diesel. By supporting heavy-duty electric trucks and dedicated charging infrastructure along critical transport routes, we’re helping bring cleaner air and quieter streets along freight corridors in Virginia, Texas, California, and Arizona. The permanent, open access charging stations will support other commercial fleets along the corridor. Our long-term purchase agreement with MacroCycle Technologies is enabling the financing of their first commercial plant in the Southeastern US, which aims to divert hard-to-recycle plastic waste from landfills and local incinerators into 5,000 tons per year of high-value recycled PET. Long-term commitments to future lower carbon production help build American industrial capacity. By focusing these efforts domestically, where we are actively expanding our data center footprint, we help anchor new projects where domestic supply of clean materials and services are limited today. The benefits are tangible and local to the communities where our partners operate. Across planned and expanded US plants, this work is estimated to support hundreds of jobs across construction and long-term manufacturing. We use a range of tools to address emissions across our direct operations, energy footprint, and supply chain. Since 2020, we’ve matched 100% of our annual electricity use with clean and renewable energy, and we continuously work to reduce the emissions through efficient design, extending the life of hardware, reusing server equipment, and prioritizing recycled materials. While we work with our suppliers to use cleaner materials and services, we’re often limited by how deep into the supply chain our influence extends and what is available on the market. These long-term purchase agreements are structured to deliver Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs), which is one way we address emissions in the most challenging sectors. With an EAC, a supplier produces verified lower carbon materials or services, Meta pays for the environmental benefit, and the material or service is used in the local market. This enables us to support lower carbon production now, and where possible, secure priority access to use these materials directly in our future data centers as new factories come online and supply chains mature. These commitments do more than secure materials and services for Meta — deploying these technologies at commercial scale helps to make them available to the entire market. That’s the outcome we are working toward: supply chains where lower carbon cement, steel, recycled plastics, and electric freight are standard options for any builder. We invite more buyers to build these markets with us. To learn more about our purchase agreements and other sustainability work, head to our sustainability website .

sources.title: US data center power demand outpaces supply by 10x
sources.text: The AI boom is facing a massive bottleneck The demand for power from the US data center boom is currently outstripping current capacity by ten times, with many developments looking for alternative sources of energy to keep their hardware online and the AI boom… booming. But with Democrats now in control of the House and Senate, the Trump administration may encounter some obstacles in continuing its attempts to turn on dirty sources of power while exempting them from environmental controls . Some AI companies have taken matters into their own hands, spinning up onsite gas turbine generators or decommissioned nuclear reactors , with a $25 billion debt on the health of Americans left to future generations to solve. The huge surge in AI demand requires billions in infrastructural investments to continue. Similar to the dot com boom where the main bottleneck was fibre cabling, the current bottleneck for AI is energy. A new report from insurance broker Howden estimates that in order to continue the current rate of data center expansion without increasing grid usage, up to 58% of power demand will need to be sourced from alternative sources. Looking at data from the US Energy Information Administration and the S&P Global since the year 2000, Howden found that data center power demand has increased by 19% year on year, while actual electricity grid expansion has only increased by 2% each year. Total grid capacity from data centers in 2025 reached 5%, whereas in 2000 it was just 0.1%. While there is significant demand on hardware for data centers — which has caused computer components such as GPUs and RAM to skyrocket — new supply chains and manufacturing is expected to ease constraints by late 2027 or early 2028. But the current growth of data center power demand could halt new data center construction by 2030, as highlighted by a Gartner report in June . Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more. Grid expansion is typically funded through ratepayers, meaning the price rises experienced by working class Americans are going towards funding new grid expansions and connections for data centers, leading experts to predict power costs in some states could rise by as much as 50% by 2030 . There are a number of alternative sources of energy that data centers are considering. Anthropic recently revealed that it is investing $3.4 billion in onsite gas turbine generators to supply the power necessary to get new sites online, but that has its own issues. In this case, Anthropic may be trading one energy crisis for another. In dodging the lack of grid capacity by turning to turbine generators, the AI company has found itself heavily reliant on natural gas supplies . The conflict in the Middle East hasn’t helped at all in this regard as other industries turn away from supply constraints placed on oil and increase their consumption of natural gas, spiking the price across the board. Gas turbine generators are not popular alternatives for those living in close proximity to data centers. Given how much power some hyperscale sites consume, some data center campuses have been equipped with ranks of gas turbine generators that emit sound levels comparable to an international airport, and the low hum has caused unexplained illnesses in local residents . Other AI companies are turning towards nuclear power to get their data centers online. Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan, Crane Clean Energy Center in Pennsylvania, and Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa are set to receive a total of $4.4 billion in federal grants to be recommissioned, with Microsoft and Google first in line to receive energy from the sites . Amazon is looking to purchase over 960 megawatts of energy from 12 small modular reactors planned to be constructed in Iowa at a cost that will likely exceed $1 billion, but the sites are yet to be approved and may not be operational until the mid-2030s. To that end, the US has just recently approved plans for the first data center-specific small nuclear reactor to provide power in Tennessee, with each modular reactor providing up to 300MW. But nuclear power is not a simple solution to the constraints placed on the US energy grid. New reactors are expensive to build, and recommissioning existing reactors requires significant investment to ensure the lifespan of a facility will meet the expected operating lifetime, with billions of dollars needed to ensure old facilities meet new and existing safety requirements. Continuing data center expansion, and the AI boom for that matter, will therefore require billions more to be invested. recent_posts.title: Falha no Grok Build, da SpaceXSI, expõe dados de milhares de usuários
recent_posts.summary: Pesquisadores encontraram mais de 35 mil aplicativos abertos ao público por um problema no desenho dos links de compartilhamento da ferramenta.

recent_posts.title: DeepMind usa IA para provar matematicamente que o protocolo do Signal é seguro
recent_posts.summary: Pesquisadores do Google usaram agentes de IA para verificar formalmente partes da criptografia que protege o Signal, o WhatsApp e o Google Messages, segundo a Wired e a ZDNet.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic reduz meta do IPO para US$ 1,4 tri, mas leva US$ 26 bi de gigantes
recent_posts.summary: Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft e TSMC Partners vão comprar ações da Anthropic fora da oferta pública, segundo a Fortune e a Business Insider.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic inicia roadshow do IPO e mira a Nasdaq como "ANT"
recent_posts.summary: Empresa oferece 825 milhões de ações Classe A entre US$ 70 e US$ 78 cada, segundo comunicado próprio e a SiliconANGLE.

recent_posts.title: Trump confirma que FBI investiga caso de Huang; Nvidia é processada
recent_posts.summary: Presidente defendeu o executivo-chefe da Nvidia após caso extraconjugal com suposta espiã chinesa, enquanto acionistas processam a empresa por declarações enganosas.

recent_posts.title: Google libera Gemini 4 Carbon para uso geral e lança o /swarm
recent_posts.summary: O modelo mais forte do Google deixa de ser restrito a testes de cibersegurança e ganha recurso que coordena vários agentes de IA ao mesmo tempo, segundo a DeepMind.

recent_posts.title: Google lança chips TPU 8tx e 8i Max para agentes de IA
recent_posts.summary: Os novos aceleradores miram segurança de dados e memória para contextos maiores, segundo a Canaltech e a TecMundo.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic lança Claude Fable 5.2 e Mythos 5.2, mais baratos
recent_posts.summary: Novos modelos custam 20% menos que o GPT-6 Astra da OpenAI e já estão na AWS, no Google Cloud e na Azure, segundo a Anthropic e a Fortune.

recent_posts.title: Ações da Nvidia caem após Huang admitir caso extraconjugal
recent_posts.summary: Fortune e TechRadar registram queda no valor de mercado da empresa depois que o executivo-chefe reconheceu relação com mulher apontada como suspeita de espionagem para a China.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia lança quatro modelos abertos para simular mundos e estradas
recent_posts.summary: Checkpoints da família Cosmos 3 geram vídeo e dados de LiDAR sincronizados para treinar robôs e carros autônomos, segundo a empresa.

recent_posts.title: Congresso dos EUA pede reunião reservada com CEO da Nvidia
recent_posts.summary: Parlamentares republicanos querem ouvir Jensen Huang sobre protocolos de segurança contra espionagem, depois do caso da suposta espiã chinesa.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia abre investigação interna sobre Jensen Huang e espionagem
recent_posts.summary: Conselho da fabricante de chips abriu apuração própria depois que um memorando de inteligência apontou executiva chinesa recrutada para se aproximar do executivo-chefe, segundo TechCrunch e CNBC.

recent_posts.title: Together AI lança compilador que usa IA para acelerar modelos
recent_posts.summary: Together Compiler usa agentes de inteligência artificial para ajustar automaticamente o código de inferência e já roda em produção, segundo a própria empresa.

recent_posts.title: IBM Research treina modelo de IA de 20B para montar slides
recent_posts.summary: Modelo pequeno e de pesos abertos usa dois papéis internos para desenhar apresentações no padrão visual de quem o treina.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI vale US$ 1,25 trilhão em nova rodada, abaixo da meta
recent_posts.summary: Avaliação ficou abaixo do teto buscado pela empresa, no mesmo momento em que a Anthropic protocolou o pedido de abertura de capital, segundo TechCrunch e The Verge.

recent_posts.title: Meta lança recurso que deixa usuários criarem mini-apps dentro do Muse
recent_posts.summary: Função chamada "spaces" permite montar painéis personalizados descrevendo a ideia em texto, segundo a Meta.

recent_posts.title: Manifestantes invadem canteiro de data center da Microsoft em Amsterdã
recent_posts.summary: Cerca de 100 pessoas entraram no canteiro de obras perto da capital holandesa nesta sexta-feira, segundo a Reuters.

recent_posts.title: Perplexity lança Teammates, agentes de IA para o trabalho
recent_posts.summary: Recurso é exclusivo do plano Max, de US$ 200 por mês, e funciona dentro do Perplexity Computer 24 horas por dia, segundo o The Verge e o Engadget.
